strengths: Addresses genuine efficiency problem in RL training with clear practical motivation
Novel DFS-based dynamic traversal algorithm that avoids quadratic memory of naive tree attention
Substantial measured improvements: 8.31× single-worker speedup with >50% memory reduction
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with detailed ablation studies on multiple model sizes
Well-structured systems contribution with load-balanced distributed training strategy
Strong presentation with clear illustrations and well-organized technical sections
Demonstrates training stability without compromising convergence
weaknesses: Critical missing comparison: No empirical evaluation against Tree Training [5], the most directly related prior work on tree-based RL training
Limited evaluation scope: Single benchmark (τ²-bench), single model family (QWEN-3), single algorithm (PPO)—generalization unclear
Fairness of baseline comparison: AREAL-DTA vs AREAL use different optimal parallel configurations in Table 1; unclear if AREAL was equally optimized
Incomplete technical analysis: Chunked backpropagation overhead claimed 'minimal' without quantification; greedy DFS ordering lacks justification
Missing analysis of when prefix sharing helps: No sensitivity study on branching factor or prefix overlap degree in evaluated workloads
Formal correctness proof absent: Gradient accumulation at shared prefix nodes is intuitively sound but lacks formal verification that results match standard training
Load-balanced partitioning algorithm: O(N log C(T)) complexity stated but partition quality relative to optimal not characterized
Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; heavy dependence on recent AReaL framework; some hyperparameter choices underspecified

strengths: Sound technical approach: DFS-based dynamic traversal effectively reduces memory overhead from O(total_tree_tokens) to O(longest_path) while maintaining correct gradient accumulation
Comprehensive system design with multiple optimizations: DFS ordering (Algorithm 1), chunked backpropagation (Algorithm 3), and load-balanced partitioning (Algorithm 4) are well-engineered
Thorough experimental evaluation on multiple model sizes (1.7B-14B) with detailed ablations isolating each component's contribution
Significant single-GPU throughput gains (up to 8.31×) and >50% peak memory reduction on high-compression workloads
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (especially Figure 2) and complete pseudocode in appendices
Honest limitations discussion: low-compression experiments (Table 3) clearly show method boundary conditions where it underperforms
weaknesses: Incremental novelty over concurrent Tree Training work (Wang et al., 2025a): core insight is an engineering alternative (dynamic traversal vs. packed tree execution) rather than a fundamentally new perspective
Large gap between single-GPU (8.31×) and end-to-end (1.28-2.28×) speedups indicates pipeline bottlenecks unresolved; root causes not deeply investigated
Severely limited applicability: benefits disappear for low-compression workloads (C≤1.5); reverses to 0.58-0.94× speedup on smaller models with weak prefix sharing
Narrow experimental scope: single primary benchmark (τ²-bench); low-compression tests use synthetic or distinct datasets; missing direct empirical comparison with Tree Training
Gradient computation correctness lacks formal proof: interleaving of forward/backward passes through complex tree structures deserves rigorous analysis beyond intuitive argument
FWD-NOGRAD overhead characterized only on τ²-bench (~7%); could vary significantly with tree structure but sensitivity analysis absent
Sparse baseline (FlexAttention) implemented by authors rather than canonical Tree Training; fairness of comparison not established
Specific to AReaL framework: generalization to other asynchronous RL systems (Laminar, HybridFlow) unclear
Code not provided for review despite promises; some experimental details missing (exact hyperparameter sweeps, rollout characteristics beyond τ²)
Insufficient analysis of practical deployment interactions: how does method work with activation recomputation? longer-horizon agentic tasks?
